Marissa — summary + attachments below. Attaching the sanitized runbook and the retention matrix.

Quick summary (suitable to send to BrightBank):
- Default retention (hosted API):
  • Raw requests (user inputs / prompt text): retained for 30 days by default.
  • Streamed fragments (intermediate fragments emitted during streaming): buffered transiently and retained for 7 days; streaming fragments are not indexed and are purged automatically by background GC jobs.
  • Final model outputs (generated completions / final transcripts): retained for 90 days by default to support troubleshooting and quality monitoring.
- Customer controls: Customers can opt into shorter windows or request immediate erasure via the account portal or by submitting an erasure request to security@redwood.com.

Proof-of-deletion we provide for erasure requests:
- Deletion job record: a job id and timestamp from our infra orchestration system that initiated object lifecycle deletion.
- Storage markers: S3 delete markers or tombstone records (object key prefix + deletedAt) for the affected storage prefix.
- Audit trail: CloudTrail-style events showing the delete API calls and the user/service principal that triggered them.
- Hash validation: when requested, we can include object checksums prior-to-deletion and subsequent verifiable logs.

Attached items: redwood_proof_of_deletion_runbook.pdf (sanitized example runbook with redacted keys) and retention_matrix_2027-11.csv (mapping of artifact types to retention windows).

Notes/limitations:
- For Dedicated and Private deployments we show the same procedural evidence, but storage residency and deletion timing can differ (on-prem timelines depend on customer ops).
- For streaming-only fragments (7-day buffer) evidence will show a GC batch job id and internal retention metrics rather than long-lived S3 objects.

Let me know if you want me to generate a one-off sample bundle for BrightBank (we can produce a sanitized PDF with job ids and CloudTrail snippets).

—Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Hi Lina — following up with the answers and an offer to provide a sanitized evidence bundle. See the short answers below (copying Kimberly for reference):

Default retention (hosted API) — short bullets you can share with your security team:
- Raw requests (prompts/user input): 30 days by default.
- Streamed fragments (in-flight tokens): buffered for 7 days, then purged via GC jobs; not indexed.
- Final model outputs (completed responses): 90 days by default for troubleshooting and quality monitoring.

What we can provide as deletion evidence (samples available):
- Deletion job id + timestamp from infra orchestration (e.g., job 'erasure-20271202-1347').
- S3 delete markers / tombstone entries showing object keys + deletedAt timestamps.
- Audit events (CloudTrail-style) showing the delete API invocation and service principal.
- Optional checksum snapshot (pre-delete) when customers request cryptographic verification.

Action items & ETA:
- Kimberly can generate a sanitized example evidence bundle (runbook excerpt + CloudTrail snippets + a redacted S3 delete marker list). We can deliver that by Friday EOD PT (2027-12-03).
- If you need a formal attestation letter, we can route the request to legal — please let me know.

Would you like the evidence bundle only, or would you prefer a short (15min) handoff call with Kimberly to walk through the artifacts?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
